name: Miyanosaka
tagline: Shinjuku in 24 minutes and Shibuya in 26 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Setagaya City, where Tokyu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 43 minutes to Otemachi, 24 minutes to Shinjuku, 26 minutes to Shibuya and 52 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 34.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 6.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 34.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 33.1 m to 40 m, a difference of 6.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 5 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: ピーコックストア 経堂店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 15 clinics and 16 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 菊池外科病院, about 12 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is さくら会世田谷中央病院, about 14 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyu Setagaya Line.
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyu Setagaya Line. It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. schools and parks within walking distance and quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kamimachi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Miyanosaka is ahead on the number of medical facilities and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Miyanosaka. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Miyanosaka.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 4 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 9 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Setagaya Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
